case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers qualification planning, registration strategy, and final Bluetooth SIG listing activities for five product registrations. A key discussion concerns reuse of Zephyr-based Controller and Host Subsystem qualifications, qualification impacts introduced by the post-July-2024 registration workflow, and handling of registration consistency checks. The exchange progresses from pre-sales qualification assessment through quotation, registration preparation, review-page validation, declaration submission, and final SDoC issuance. The thread also confirms post-registration compliance obligations for the Listing Owner.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The primary technical discussion concerns qualification of products using Zephyr-based Bluetooth implementations and reuse of existing Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem qualifications. The consultant explains that products using Zephyr and no SIG-defined profile implementation can qualify through declaration using existing qualified subsystem references, while SIG profile implementations may require additional Profile Subsystem qualification evidence. A separate issue arises when combining a specific RF PHY qualification with existing Zephyr Controller and Host subsystem references, causing GAP ICS inconsistencies under updated check rules. The consultant explains that correcting the ICS would trigger protocol test requirements for the modified layer, creating practical qualification difficulties. During final registration, yellow warning indicators appear on the Review Page because a Host layer is not included, but these warnings do not block submission and the registrations remain acceptable.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Qualification eligibility depends on whether the implementation remains within the scope of existing qualified subsystem designs and whether any profile functionality or ICS modifications introduce new qualification obligations. Existing Zephyr Controller and Host subsystem qualifications can be reused when the implementation remains within their qualified feature scope. However, when qualification data modifications are required to resolve ICS inconsistencies, the modified layer becomes subject to additional qualification requirements and associated testing obligations. Review Page warnings must be evaluated based on their meaning; informational warnings that do not represent qualification rule failures do not prevent successful submission.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Selecting an inappropriate qualification composition or modifying ICS data without understanding qualification consequences can trigger additional protocol testing requirements that may be difficult or impossible for parties lacking stack-source ownership. Reusing qualifications outside their qualified feature scope can result in invalid qualification assumptions and registration issues. Misinterpreting informational Review Page warnings as blocking errors can create unnecessary delays. Failure to maintain the required compliance folder after registration can create audit and compliance exposure if the Bluetooth SIG requests supporting records.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: An earlier assessment assumed a qualification structure using existing Zephyr Controller and Host subsystem references and therefore concluded that no additional issues would occur. After reviewing the actual intended registration composition, which incorporated a different RF PHY qualification reference, the consultant discovered GAP ICS inconsistencies that changed the qualification analysis. The mistake was incomplete verification of the exact referenced qualification structure during the earlier assessment. The correction was to recreate the intended registration in a project workspace, identify the resulting ICS issues, and provide an updated qualification recommendation.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always validate the exact qualification composition, including all referenced QDIDs, subsystem layers, RF PHY substitutions, and intended registration structure, in a qualification workspace before providing final qualification guidance. Small changes in referenced designs can alter consistency-check outcomes, trigger additional testing obligations, and change the recommended qualification path.
